question: Does repeated computation within a fixed latent state resolve additional interactions without conventional move search?
registration: Before corpus generation and lane measurements
depth_definition: All incidence input is available from round zero; subsequent rounds reuse or compose internal state. No additional target or move is revealed per round.
random_sampling: Rejection sample equal positive/negative labels per size/split; density drawn uniformly from 0.15,0.25,0.4,0.55,0.7,0.85. Distinct raw graphs throughout corpus, not an isomorphism holdout.
structure_permutations: Up to 8 distinct coherent target/resource permutations per template or pair, at most 128 attempts; structural rows reserved before random sampling
oracle: Offline Hall-deficiency formula for maximum matching, independently checked by resource-subset dynamic programming on every corpus row
learning: TRAIN fits, DEV checkpoint selection only. EVAL and STRUCTURE measured only after all model checkpoints frozen. Separate size/family metrics.
interpretation: Algebraic interaction order, local message propagation radius, and learned recurrent inference are different meanings of latent depth and must be reported separately. Extra rounds are not assumed to improve accuracy.
